transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-08-05 11:00 AM PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Singh (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Riley Torres (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (Lakeside), Tess Monroe (Lakeside CTO), Samir Gupta (Lakeside Platform), Ava Reynolds (Lakeside Security)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards and cost breakdown. Customer concerned about per-route unit economics, multi-tenant routing, and private deployment networking / encryption. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send pricing + SOW, SE to run a benchmark on sample prompts, Lakeside to share traffic profile/VPC details.

Topics: Usage analytics, per-route dashboards, token-level cost, KV cache/prefix caching, dedicated vs hosted, VPC/SAML/KMS, trial/pilot scope

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick us off, this is Maya from Redwood inference, with Ethan and Riley from our solutions engineering team. can you hear ok on your side jordan?
[00:18] Jordan: yeah loud and clear, thanks. Tess is on and ava and samir as well, we wanted to see the console usage analytics and how you break down cost per route, that was the ask from procurement.
[00:30] Maya: perfect, we'll jump into the console. a quick note: demo environment data is synthetic but maps to the same dashboards you'd see in prod. i'll share the deck and the console link after.
[00:45] Ethan: opening the per-route dashboard now — top left is global overview: total tokens, cost, avg latency, error rate. you can filter by model, route, time window, and tenant id.
[01:12] Tess: when you say route, is that per-endpoint path? like our billing routes?
[01:22] Ethan: exactly. we map routes to API routes or logical product features. so you can see cost for route /chat/summary vs /embed/search and roll up into team-level views.
[01:40] Riley: one thing to call out — token-level cost is broken down into model compute, inference overhead (eg: batching/overhead), and infra amortization. that third piece is where dedicated pools change the numbers.
[02:05] Samir: how do you show caching impact? our prompts have heavy prefix repetition so we need to understand savings.
[02:17] Ethan: good question — we surface cache hits as a separate metric. the per-route view shows cache hit rate and estimated token savings from prefix/K V cache. note: transcription may show as K V cache or KV cach in some internal logs.
[02:40] Jordan: can we see example rows? like tokens saved and dollars saved per day?
[02:50] Ethan: yep, scrolling the table — column 'tokens_raw' 'tokens_saved_by_cache' and 'est_cost_delta_usd'. you can sort, group, and export CSV.
[03:12] Tess: export is important for our finance team. do you support CSV and direct S3 export?
[03:22] Maya: yes CSV today, and we can push reports to a customer S3 bucket for Dedicated/Private customers.
[03:35] Ava: security question — how are logs encrypted and who has access? do you have audit logs, retention controls, and KMS?
[03:48] Riley: we support KMS integration and HSM-backed keys on Private. audit logs are available in the console activity pane and can be forwarded to your SIEM. RBAC integrates with SAML/SSO, and we have per-role granularity.
[04:10] Ava: SOC2? certs?
[04:15] Maya: yes SOC2 Type II, and we'll attach our compliance pack in the follow-up email.
[04:24] Samir: on cost — show us how quantization changes unit economics.
[04:32] Ethan: switching to the 'optimize' tab — we recommend quantization profiles by model and by route. the console simulates quality vs cost tradeoffs using your eval set if you upload one. there's a recommended profile: 8-bit dynamic, 4-bit for low-fidelity routes, and we surface an estimated delta.
[04:58] Jordan: how accurate is the estimate? we've seen big differences in other tools.
[05:06] Riley: it depends on your token distribution and sequence lengths; we run a quick simulated pass on a subset to give a conservative estimate. for pilots we recommend an actual benchmark on a dedicated node — which Ethan can run.
[05:26] Ethan: i'll take that as an action item, we'll run 50k token sim and return a spreadsheet with latency and cost-per-1k-token numbers.
[05:40] Tess: routing policies — can we route by latency SLO or cost constraints? we want critical routes in low-latency tier and cheaper routes on preemptible.
[05:54] Maya: yes, smart routing supports policy rules: latency-first, cost-first, region preference, and can fallback to compatible model variants when capacity is low. we showed an example policy earlier in the deck.
[06:10] Jordan: there's mention of per-token chargebacks to product teams — can we tag routes with owner metadata?
[06:18] Ethan: absolutely. routes and models accept tags; you can allocate cost to owners and set monthly budgets/alerts per tag.
[06:30] Samir: networking — for Private deployment how does VPC peering / egress work? do you require open ports?
[06:40] Riley: Private offering uses customer VPC with a customer-managed peering or Transit Gateway; we provide a control plane endpoint and a private data plane. we can send a network diagram; Samir if you share your CIDR and peering requirements we can validate.
[06:58] Samir: will do. latency is key for us — our production SLO is 200ms p50 for chat. can Redwood meet that?
[07:08] Ethan: with dedicated pools and optimized kernels, p50 at 200ms for short contexts (<=512 tokens) is achievable on token-optimized models. for long contexts or larger models we'll dimension nodes differently.
[07:28] Tess: anything about pre-warming or KV cache priming? we have bursts at 9am every day.
[07:36] Ethan: yes autoscaling and pre-warming policies exist; you can schedule capacity or use traffic-aware burst capacity. KV cache priming is supported via warm-up requests or persistent sessions.
[07:54] Jordan: what's the expected ROI if we migrate 3 high-traffic routes to Redwood dedicated? rough numbers please.
[08:02] Maya: based on similar customers we typically see 25-45% lower unit cost at scale due to batching, prefix caching, and quantization. we'll refine that after the benchmark.
[08:18] Ava: curious about PII — do you do redact at rest or is that on the app side?
[08:26] Riley: we recommend app-side redaction, but for Private we can enable redaction pipelines and tokenization hooks before storage. logs can be redacted before leaving the VPC.
[08:42] Jordan: can we link with our billing system to show per-product chargebacks?
[08:47] Ethan: yes you'll get CSV exports and APIs for usage; many customers connect to internal chargeback jobs.
[09:00] Tess: show me the per-route cost timeline again — the graph on the right.
[09:05] Ethan: sure, zooming in — this spike corresponds to a burst where caching missed; you can click the spike and it surfaces sample requests, prompt sizes, and model used.
[09:26] Jordan: that's useful to debug regressions. can we set regression alerts on quality metrics?
[09:31] Riley: yes, quality monitoring ties to eval sets and prompt groups; we can alert on metric drift and regression versus a baseline.
[09:46] Maya: also worth noting rollouts: you can do canary or A/B and automatic fallback to previous model if latency or quality regress.
[09:58] Samir: procurement question — what options for committed capacity and discounts?
[10:05] Maya: Dedicated offers reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits, and the bigger the commitment the deeper the discount. we typically propose a pilot commit for 3 months.
[10:18] Tess: security pack needed — can you share SOC2, pen test, and data flow doc?
[10:25] Maya: yes we'll attach the compliance pack; action item for me to include SOC2 report and pen test summary.
[10:36] Jordan: what's timeline to start a pilot? can we do a two-week pilot with the benchmark + integration?
[10:44] Maya: yes typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: benchmarking, integration to your staging, and then production smoke tests.
[10:52] Ethan: one more detail — console supports per-route quotas and throttles. we can set soft/hard limits and alert teams when they approach thresholds.
[11:05] Samir: about data retention — we need 90 day retention for logs and 365 for audit. can you configure that?
[11:12] Riley: retention is configurable; audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM for long-term storage.
[11:22] Tess: fine. last question on multi-tenant isolation — if we have multiple product teams on same account can one team see another's usage?
[11:31] Ethan: with RBAC and per-route tagging you can restrict visibility; for stronger isolation Dedicated offers isolated pools and Private offers full network/tenancy separation.
[11:45] Jordan: ok great. next steps?
[11:50] Maya: recap: we'll send pricing and SOW, attach security docs; ethan will run the benchmark after they send sample prompts; samir to send network diagram; schedule pilot kickoff next week.
[12:10] Tess: sounds good, thanks all.

(Transcript ends — meeting closed at ~11:45 AM PDT)
